submission.justification: Simulation shows D3 gives the highest light yield at every coverage. At 30% coverage, the maximum allowed and the feedthrough limit, D3 gives 51.4 PE/MeV. D2 gives 37.5 and D1 gives 25.6, so D3 is about 37% above D2. No design has a documented cryogenic failure, but none has cryogenic qualification data either. The D3 thin bonded filter is flagged as unverified for robustness. Robustness matters because modules are inaccessible once the cryostat is filled, so this is a real risk. It is unresolved, not a demonstrated failure. I recommend D3 at 30% on the strength of the light-yield goal, with D2 at 30% (37.5 PE/MeV) as the fallback. D3 should receive cryogenic qualification of the filter bonding before the design is committed.
